profile.main_concern:
I've been exhausted for six months and my heart races when I climb stairs. I can't concentrate at work. My stomach has been bloated and sore. Each doctor looked at one thing and said it was probably fine.

Symptoms: Fatigue (about 6 months): Need a nap after work; worse in the afternoon.; Heart racing / palpitations (about 4 months): Mostly on stairs or walking fast. Sometimes lightheaded when I stand up.; Brain fog / trouble concentrating (about 3 months): Losing my train of thought in meetings.; Bloating and upper stomach discomfort (about 3 months): Burning feeling after meals, better with food some days.; Headaches (about 1 year): Most days; I take ibuprofen almost every day.; Craving ice (a few months): I chew ice all day.; Heavier periods (about 1 year): Periods are heavier than they used to be.; Feeling cold and hair shedding (a few months)

My questions: Are my heart racing, tiredness and stomach problems connected? Should I still be taking ibuprofen? Is my thyroid OK?
doctors: Family medicine (primary care) - Dr. Laura Chen

summary.plain_language_summary: Your blood tests show low iron and a low blood count, which may help explain the tiredness, ice chewing, lightheadedness, and racing heart. Your heart tests showed a faster-than-usual rhythm, but the ultrasound was reassuring and no sustained rhythm problem was identified. The positive stool blood test still needs the recommended colonoscopy, and your stomach exam found erosions and a small ulcer; biopsy results are pending. Frequent ibuprofen use is important to review with your doctors because the endoscopy report advised avoiding it and you have stomach findings and low iron. Your thyroid test was only slightly outside the reference range, with free T4 in range, so planned repeat testing can clarify it.

key_findings.text: Blood tests show low hemoglobin with small red blood cells and very low iron stores.
The stool test was positive for blood, and the recommended colonoscopy has not yet been scheduled.
The endoscopy found stomach erosions and a small ulcer without active bleeding at the time; biopsy results are pending.
The H. pylori stool test was positive; the plan is to be addressed after pathology is available.
Heart monitoring and ECG recorded a fast rhythm, while the heart ultrasound showed normal pumping function and no significant valve problem.
TSH was mildly high while free T4 was in range; repeat thyroid testing is planned.
Heavier periods, cold sensitivity, hair shedding, and frequent ice chewing are reported and worth discussing alongside the test results.

connections.text: The low iron and anemia may contribute to fatigue, lightheadedness, and exertional racing heart; these symptoms should not be attributed only to the mildly raised TSH.
Low iron and a positive stool blood test make completing the recommended colon evaluation important; the stomach findings and pending biopsy also need follow-up.
Frequent ibuprofen use is relevant to the stomach erosions and ulcer, positive stool blood test, and low iron, and should be discussed with the clinicians managing these findings.
Heavier periods may also be relevant when discussing low iron and anemia with the gynecologist and care team.
Cold sensitivity and hair shedding can be raised alongside the mildly high TSH and normal free T4, while recognizing the separate low-iron findings.
